definitions.explanation: The physical act of standing on tiptoe or stretching one's body upward to reach something or see over something.

definitions.gloss: overreaching, trying to appear bigger or better than one is
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, trying to act beyond one's actual ability, status, or means. Attempting to appear more mature, sophisticated, or capable than one really is.

examples.japanese: {背伸|せの}びして{棚|たな}の{上|うえ}に{手|て}を{伸|の}ばした。
examples.english: I stood on tiptoe and reached for the top of the shelf.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{背伸|せの}びをして{窓|まど}の{外|そと}をのぞいている。
examples.english: The child is standing on tiptoe, peeking out the window.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}、{大|おお}きく{背伸|せの}びをすると{気持|きも}ちがいい。
examples.english: It feels good to have a big stretch in the morning.

examples.japanese: {背伸|せの}びせずに{自然体|しぜんたい}でいたい。
examples.english: I want to be natural and not try to be something I'm not.

examples.japanese: {高|たか}いレストランに{行|い}くのは{少|すこ}し{背伸|せの}びだった。
examples.english: Going to an expensive restaurant was a bit of a stretch for us.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}は{背伸|せの}びして{大人|おとな}ぶっていたが、{今|いま}は{等身大|とうしんだい}の{自分|じぶん}を{大切|たいせつ}にしている。
examples.english: When I was young I used to act more grown-up than I was, but now I value being my true self.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is very common in everyday conversation. It is not necessarily negative — sometimes {背伸|せの}び is seen as a healthy aspiration, though it more often implies overreaching.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {背伸|せの}びをする (stand on tiptoe; overreach)
- {背伸|せの}びしない (not overreach, be natural)
- {少|すこ}し{背伸|せの}び (a little bit of a stretch)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- つま{先立|さきだ}ち: standing on tiptoe (purely physical)
- {無理|むり}をする: push oneself too hard, overdo it (stronger negative nuance)
